column3: NASB treats “I had wearied myself to relent” as present, “I am tired of relenting.”
NASB renders the Hebrew past tenses (“I have winnowed … I have made childless”) as future.
NASB renders the Hebrew past tenses as future (“will be,” “will bring”).
The Hebrew “I will set you free” follows the reading tradition; the sentence is difficult and the meaning is uncertain.
“Will it break iron” is rendered “Can anyone smash iron.”
“I will make pass your enemies” is rendered “cause your enemies to bring it”; many manuscripts read “I will make you serve.”
“To the length of your anger” is rendered “in view of Your patience.”
“Your name is called on me” is rendered “I have been called by Your name.”
